findings.title: Rejected devices are cached as successfully tagged
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` adds the device ID to the local cache before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` enforces the configured limit. When a new device is rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, its cache entry remains for the cache TTL; a subsequent request with the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id` returns early at line 83 without touching the store, so `Authenticate` sees no error and permits anonymous access. Set the cache entry only after a successful store write (and do not cache failed tagging attempts).

findings.title: Device limit check and insertion are not atomic
findings.body: The limit is enforced by a `COUNT` in one database session followed by an upsert in another session. Concurrent requests can all observe a count below `deviceLimit` and then each insert a distinct device ID, exceeding the configured limit; this also occurs across Grafana instances. The count/check/insert needs database-level serialization or an atomic conditional insert/transaction with appropriate locking.
